knowledge_graph.title: Major Diagnostic Category
knowledge_graph.description: The Major Diagnostic Categories are formed by dividing all possible principal diagnoses into 25 mutually exclusive diagnosis areas. MDC codes, like diagnosis-related group codes, are primarily a claims and administrative data element unique to the United States medical care reimbursement system.

related_questions.question: What does MDC mean in medical terms?

text_blocks.snippet: In medical terms, MDC typically stands for Major Diagnostic Category. These are broad groupings of diagnoses that are used to classify patients based on the primary reason for their hospital admission. MDCs are a key component of the Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Groups (MS-DRGs) system, which is used for hospital payment.

list.title: Purpose:
list.snippet: MDCs organize diagnoses into categories based on similar clinical characteristics and resource utilization.

list.title: Structure:
list.snippet: There are usually 25-27 MDCs, with each MDC corresponding to a specific body system or medical condition (e.g., diseases of the respiratory system, pregnancy and childbirth).

list.title: Usage:
list.snippet: MDCs are used as the first level of classification in the MS-DRG system, which is used by Medicare and other payers to determine hospital payment for inpatient services.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Some common MDCs include:
MDC 4: Diseases and Disorders of the Respiratory System
MDC 5: Diseases and Disorders of the Circulatory System
MDC 6: Diseases and Disorders of the Digestive System
MDC 8: Diseases and Disorders of the Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue
MDC 10: Endocrine, Nutritional, and Metabolic Diseases and Disorders

list.title: Other Meanings:
list.snippet: While less common, MDC can also refer to:
Medical Device Communications: in the context of standards like ISO/IEEE 11073-10101, according to HL7 Terminology.
Major Diagnostic Classes: in the context of ICD-10-CM coding, as mentioned by ResDAC.
Medical and Dental Council: in some regions.
Congenital Muscular Dystrophies: (MDCs).

text_blocks.snippet: However, in most medical contexts, MDC refers to Major Diagnostic Category.

related_questions.title: DRG - Medical Codes

text_blocks.snippet: Major Diagnostic Categories (MDCs) are broad classifications of diseases and conditions used in healthcare, particularly in hospital settings, to group similar diagnoses. They serve as a first level of grouping for Diagnosis Related Groups (DRGs), which are used for billing and payment. Each MDC typically corresponds to a specific organ system or a major medical condition.
snippet_highlighted_words: broad classifications of diseases and conditions used in healthcare, particularly in hospital settings, to group similar diagnoses

list.title: Grouping of Diagnoses:
list.snippet: MDCs group together diagnoses that are related to the same body system or a specific medical condition, such as the respiratory system, circulatory system, or pregnancy.

list.title: Connection to DRGs:
list.snippet: MDCs are used to organize and classify DRGs, which are used for reimbursement in hospitals.

list.title: Not Disease-Specific:
list.snippet: While MDCs relate to body systems, they are not specific to individual diseases like cancer or sepsis.

list.title: Used by Governmental Agencies:
list.snippet: Governmental agencies and researchers utilize MDCs to measure the burden of disease and allocate healthcare resources, according to Value in Health.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Some common MDCs include: diseases and disorders of the respiratory system (MDC 04), circulatory system (MDC 05), and digestive system (MDC 06).

list.title: Pre-MDC:
list.snippet: There are also categories like "Pre-MDC" which include transplants and tracheostomies, and cases where the principal procedure does not align with the principal diagnosis.
